proposals.hypothesis: LiNbF6 is a wide-gap, insulating fluoride with fully oxidized Nb(V) and charge-balanced Li(I). Its F-rich anion should resist oxidation at the LiCoO2 interface near 4 V and avoid the oxide-type P/S oxidation products seen with Li3PO4 and Li2ZrO3. It extends the fluoride family that has given the lowest penalties (LiF about 0.057, Li2SiF6 about 0.076, Li2TiF6 about 0.081), with a high-valent, larger Nb(V) center that may shift the contact product set.
proposals.motivation: Fluorides with high-valent cations consistently gave lower contact penalties than the oxides (Li3PO4 bin 28, Li2ZrO3 bin 16), with LiF at bin 2, Li2SiF6 at bin 3 and Li2TiF6 at bin 4. LiNbF6 is an unexplored Li–M(V)–F composition in this family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-ion conductor that is chemically compatible with the PS4/PS5 sulfide framework (shared P-O/P-S chemistry), and its oxidative stability is reasonable at the LiCoO2 interface near 4 V. It is a standard LiPON-like coating choice for suppressing sulfide/oxide interfacial decomposition.

Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, electrically insulating lithium-ion conductor with a highly oxidized Zr(IV) center. Its oxide framework should resist oxidation at the LiCoO2 interface near 4 V. Zr-O bonds are strong, so it should be less prone than Li3PO4 to releasing P/S/Cl-containing products when in contact with Li6PS5Cl. Li2ZrO3 is a commonly used sulfide-compatible cathode coating, so it is a chemically different family from the phosphate tested so far.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was insulating with a wide gap but had contact penalty 0.337 eV/atom (bin 16), with the sulfide contact decomposing to P2O5, SCl4 and SO2. A non-phosphate lithium oxide with a stable high-valent metal is expected to show less contact reactivity.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-ion-conducting fluoride. Its F(-I) anion is hard to oxidize, so it should resist decomposition at the LiCoO2 interface near 4 V. Both oxide coatings tested so far (Li3PO4, Li2ZrO3) were penalized by sulfide-side reactions that released P2O5, SO2 and SCl4, which points to oxygen-rich oxides as the weak point. A fluoride should be less oxidizing toward the PS4/PS5 framework, so it is a chemically distinct family to test for lower contact penalty.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (penalty 0.574, bin 28) and Li2ZrO3 (penalty 0.337, bin 16) both showed oxidative sulfide-side decomposition at the Li6PS5Cl contact, so an oxide-free halide coating is the next logical family to test.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3AlF6 is a wide-gap, insulating fluoride with a fully oxidized, strongly bound Al(III)-F framework. It is Li-rich and should be less prone than the oxides to releasing S/P oxidation products at the Li6PS5Cl contact. It is a close analogue of the LiF result (penalty 0.31, bin 15), with Al-F bonding expected to be more thermodynamically robust than the simple LiF product set.
